runs.question: A ServiceNow GlideRecord script using addEncodedQuery returned every record when the encoded query had a typo in a field name. Why does that happen, and is there a system property that changes it? Answer briefly and cite your sources with URLs.
runs.final_answer:
ServiceNow **drops the invalid query condition** and executes the remaining valid conditions. If the misspelled field was your only filter, this effectively becomes an unfiltered query and can return every record. [GlideRecord documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideRecordScopedAPI.html)

Set **`glide.invalid_query.returns_no_rows` to `true`** to make invalid encoded queries return no records. It isn’t an absolute safeguard: ServiceNow documents exceptions involving invalid terms with a `WHERE` operator, where the remaining query can still return results. [Property behavior and caveat](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/xanadu/api-reference/server-api-reference/c_GlideRecordAPI.html)

runs.question: Our ServiceNow users get logged out after being idle. Which system property controls the idle session timeout and what is its default? Answer briefly and cite your sources with URLs.
runs.final_answer:
The property is **`glide.ui.session_timeout`**, measured in **minutes**. The default idle timeout is **30 minutes**. [ServiceNow documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-administration/user-administration/c_ManageUserSessions.html)

Technically, if the property is unset, **30 minutes is the fallback**. [Property reference](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/platform-security/instance-security-hardening-settings/sc-session-activity-timeout.html)

runs.question: Use the docs_search and docs_read tools from the sn MCP server. A ServiceNow REST client is slow because the Table API builds Link pagination headers. Is there a Table API parameter to skip them? Say which ServiceNow release your source is from, and cite it with URLs.
runs.final_answer:
Yes—add **`sysparm_suppress_pagination_header=true`** to your Table API GET request:

```http
GET /api/now/table/incident?sysparm_limit=100&sysparm_suppress_pagination_header=true
```

It suppresses the response’s `Link` pagination header; the default is `false`. Your client can still paginate using `sysparm_limit` and `sysparm_offset`.

I verified this using sn MCP’s `docs_search` and `docs_read`. The source is **ServiceNow Brazil**, updated **September 10, 2026**: [Table API documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/rest-apis/c_TableAPI.html) and [release-specific source, lines 378–391](https://github.com/ServiceNow/ServiceNowDocs/blob/brazil/markdown/api-reference/rest-apis/c_TableAPI.md#L378-L391).

The documentation confirms header suppression, but does not promise a particular performance improvement.

runs.question: Try the docs_search tool from the sn MCP server, plus whatever else is useful. Why might a ServiceNow business rule not run after an update made through GlideRecord? Answer briefly and cite your sources with URLs. (GitMCP blocked by a local preload, to simulate an outage.)

steps.web_search: site.servicenow.com business rules GlideRecord setWorkflow false conditions async

runs.final_answer:
GlideRecord updates normally trigger business rules. Check these likely causes:

- **`gr.setWorkflow(false)`** was called before `gr.update()`, suppressing business rules. [ServiceNow documentation](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/business-rules-classic/c_BusinessRules.html)
- **The rule doesn’t qualify:** verify Active, the target table, Update selected, and filter/script conditions—including whether a field actually changed when using `changes()`. [Business rule configuration](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=learning-module&identifier=SSS_About_zurich%2Cnew_to_servicenow&module=learning+plan&release=zurich)
- **It’s async:** execution may be delayed; its script cannot rely on `previous` or change-detection methods. Condition fields do support change detection. [Async rule behavior](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/api-reference/business-rules-classic/c_BusinessRules.html)
- **Recursive execution was stopped:** calling `current.update()` inside a business rule can trigger recursion detection. Check system logs. [Business rule best practices](https://developer.servicenow.com/print_page.do?category=now-platform&identifier=business_rules_technical_best_practices&module=guide&release=zurich)

I tried sn MCP’s `docs_search`; it returned `DOCS_UNAVAILABLE`, so I used ServiceNow’s web documentation.
